name: Mechanical Behavior: Yieldora
subtitle: Mechanical Behavior Materials
shortDescription: Learn why materials yield, creep, fatigue and fracture: 3D yield surfaces, dislocations, crack tips and 18 cited labs, with adaptive quizzes. Free core course.
longDescription:
Mechanical Behavior: Yieldora explains why solids bend, flow, wear out and break, and gives you the numbers to predict it. It follows an upper-level materials course, from elastic constants to fracture, and is for engineering and materials-science students.

Pick how to study. The classical view runs 14 chapters and 74 teaching points: elasticity and anisotropy, yield criteria, dislocations and strengthening, hardening and necking, fracture mechanics, fatigue crack growth, creep, statistical strength, contact, hydrogen and more. The real-world view starts from a thing to check or build, for example a pressure-vessel yield margin, and opens the lesson when the next step needs it. 19 builds and the course share one record, so switching view keeps your progress.

18 interactive labs draw on the graphics chip: drag a 3D von Mises or Tresca yield surface, tilt the plane of a 3D Mohr circle, push a dislocation through a lattice and watch it pile up, probe the stress field at a crack tip, read a creep map, grow a plastic zone or a void, trace a Weibull curve and place a point on a failure-assessment diagram. Every lab cites its relation and checks itself with an independent second method.

Practice adapts. 616 original practice questions run over four levels from Beginner to Research: 444 are calculations whose answers were each computed twice by different routes and 172 are concept items for practice. The 18 case studies add 72 more calculation parts. The app follows what you know, resurfaces what is slipping and links each miss to the lesson behind it, kindly and specifically. Choose 5, 10, 20 or 40 questions, or your own length. 18 case studies and 3 timed paper-style practice exams are included.

Coverage, stated plainly: 67 of 74 points cite a topic of an opened MIT OCW course or a NASA standard, 7 rest on encyclopedia headings only. We do not claim to cover every topic of any course or textbook; the Coverage screen lists what is not covered, such as multiaxial fatigue criteria and crystal plasticity finite elements.

Sources open in a wide sheet with Back and Close. Text can be sized from 50 to 300 percent. No sign-in, no network needed, and your progress stays on your device.

The core course is free: the classical view, quizzes at levels 1 to 3, early builds, the first labs, Coverage and your progress. One optional monthly subscription, Yieldora Plus Monthly, unlocks Plus: later build projects, labs beyond the first six, the timed practice exams, the case studies and Level 4 research questions with longer sets. Lessons, worked solutions and progress are never locked. The subscription renews monthly until cancelled in your account settings; the store shows the price before you confirm. Restore purchases is under More.

For study only; not design approval, certification or failure-investigation advice. No affiliation with any university, standards body or publisher named in the sources.
